comment: First calibration suite for tools/perf/make_synthetic_gguf.py. Data only: no measurements. expected_file_bytes is plan(spec).file_size; tests/test_synthetic_gguf.py keeps it in step. Generate one file: make_synthetic_gguf.py --arch ... --out FILE (spec keys map to the flags; quant is the matrix type). Every file sets context_length 65536: depth is a request property, the harness passes -c itself.

files.from: design B run A / design A D1
files.isolates: per-token fixed cost: c0 plus 16 layers of per-layer cost; the bytes term is far below it on a fast card
files.compare: compare with layers-48 (same width, 3x layers) and bytes-mid / bytes-large-1 (same layers, wider)

files.from: design B run C / design A D3
files.isolates: cost per layer: same width as fixed-floor, 48 layers; the weight-bytes difference is small
self-check: the fixed-floor to bytes-large-1 line must predict this file; the residual is the model-misspecification term
files.compare: same layer count as fixed-floor and bytes-large-1, width between them

files.from: design B run B (small point) / design A D2
files.isolates: weight-streaming rate: same layers as fixed-floor, about 15x the bytes, so t[large] - t[fixed-floor] = bytes / rate with the fixed part cancelled; also the base file for depth and prefill (ubatch) arms
files.compare: slope against fixed-floor and bytes-mid; resize --embd/--ff so bytes / rate is at least 3 ms on the measured device

files.isolates: second bytes point for the streaming rate (about 2x bytes-large-1); a card with more than ~0.6 TB/s needs it for a 3 ms difference
files.compare: three-point line with fixed-floor and bytes-large-1

files.from: design B run B-type (legacy class); design A T1
files.isolates: quant-type kernel cost at EQUAL weight bytes: Q4_0 and Q4_K are both 4.5 bits per weight

files.from: design B run B-type; design A T1
files.isolates: quant-type cost across a bytes change (8.5 bits per weight): bytes term predicted from bytes-large-1 plus the Q4_0 type factor
files.compare: residual of the bytes-large-1 line at 1.9x bytes

files.from: design B run B-depth / design A depth point
files.isolates: KV read cost: bytes-large-1 geometry with full multi-head KV (128 KiB of f16 KV per token of context), so the depth slope stands out
files.compare: decode at depth 0 versus 4k/16k of cached prompt on this file; also bytes-large-1 (64 KiB/token) at the same depths

files.from: design A D1 / E1 dense half
files.isolates: dense half of the equal-active-bytes pair: FFN width 2048
files.compare: against pair-moe: same attention, same weight bytes read per token (the MoE reads 2.4% more for the router)

files.from: design A E1 / design B run M1
files.isolates: cost of routed layers at equal active bytes: 32 experts of FFN width 512 (0.3 MB per expert matrix), 4 used = FFN width 2048
files.compare: (t[pair-moe] - t[pair-dense]) / 16 layers = per-layer routing and expert-gather cost

files.isolates: expert-slice size: 16 experts of FFN width 1792, 2 used (2 MB per expert matrix); slice-size saturation against pair-moe; also the hybrid CPU-expert arm
files.compare: against pair-moe: per-layer cost versus slice bytes

files.from: task: transfer to real MoE files
files.isolates: per-layer geometry of a Qwen3-30B-A3B-class model (embd 2048, 128 experts of width 768, 8 used) with 4 layers; no q/k norms
files.compare: per-layer cost here versus the per-layer cost implied by a real A3B file of the same geometry (48 layers): the transfer check
